cover.author: Jiong Sheng from London, United Kingdom

spots.name: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum is situated at the foot of the second peak of Purple Mountain in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. Construction of the tomb started in January 1926, shortly after Sun Yat-sen's death, and was finished in spring of 1929. The architect was Lü Yanzhi, who died shortly after it was finished.

spots.name: Porcelain Tower of Nanjing
spots.summary: The Porcelain Tower of Nanjing, part of the former Great Bao'en Temple, is a historical site located on the south bank of external Qinhuai River in Nanjing, China.

photo.author: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach's A Plan of Civil and Historical Architecture

spots.name: Xiao Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Ming Xiaoling is the mausoleum of the Hongwu Emperor, the founder of the Ming dynasty. It lies at the southern foot of Purple Mountain, located east of the historical centre of Nanjing.

spots.name: Zifeng Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Zifeng Tower is a 450-meter (1,480 ft) supertall skyscraper in Nanjing, Jiangsu. The 89-story building completed in 2010 comprises retail and office. Floors 49/71 feature a hotel, numerous restaurants, and a public observatory.

spots.name: Presidential Palace
spots.summary: The Presidential Palace in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China, housed the Office of the President of the Republic of China from 1927 until the capital was relocated to Taipei in 1949. It is now a museum called the China Modern History Museum. It is located at No.292 Changjiang Road, in the Xuanwu District of Nanjing.

spots.name: City Wall of Nanjing
spots.summary: The City Wall of Nanjing was designed by the Hongwu Emperor (1328–1398) after he founded the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644) and established Nanjing as the capital in 1368. To consolidate his sovereignty and defend the city against coastal pirates, he adopted the suggestion of his advisor Zhu Sheng to build a higher city wall.

spots.name: Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge
spots.summary: The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge, previously called the First Nanjing Yangtze Bridge, is a double-decked road-rail truss bridge across the Yangtze River in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China connecting the city's Pukou and Gulou districts. Its upper deck is part of China National Highway 104, spanning 4,588 metres (15,052 ft).

spots.summary: The Porcelain Tower of Nanjing, part of the former Great Bao'en Temple, is a historical site located on the south bank of external Qinhuai River in Nanjing, China.

spots.name: Nanjing Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Nanjing Museum is a provincial public museum in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. It is owned by the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government and operated by the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism.

spots.name: Nanjing Fuzimiao

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nanjing Fuzimiao or Fuzimiao, is a Confucius Temple and former site of imperial examination hall located in southern Nanjing City on banks of the Qinhuai River. It is now a popular tourist attraction with pedestrian shopping streets around the restored temple buildings.

spots.name: Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders is a museum to memorialize those that were killed in the Nanjing Massacre by the Imperial Japanese Army in and around the then-capital of China, Nanjing, after it fell on 13 December 1937.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders

spots.name: Jiming Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jiming Temple is a renowned Buddhist temple in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. One of the oldest temples in Nanjing, it is located in the Xuanwu District near Xuanwu Lake.

spots.name: Nanjing Olympic Sports Centre
spots.summary: Nanjing Olympic Sports Center Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium located in Hexi New Town, Nanjing, China.

spots.name: Ming Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ming Palace, also known as the "Forbidden City of Nanjing", was the 14th-century imperial palace of the early Ming dynasty, when Nanjing was the capital of China.

spots.name: Zhan Garden
spots.summary: Zhan Garden is a Chinese garden located on No. 128 Zhan Yuan Road, beside Fuzimiao, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.

spots.name: Yuhuatai Memorial Park of Revolutionary Martyrs
spots.summary: Yuhuatai Memorial Park of Revolutionary Martyrs (雨花台烈士陵园) is a park and tourist site in the Yuhuatai District of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China. The name Yuhuatai comes from yu (rain), hua (flower), tai (platform). A prominent feature of the park is a statue of nine figures.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Yuhuatai Memorial Park of Revolutionary Martyrs

spots.name: Linggu Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Linggu Temple is a famous Buddhist temple in Nanjing. It is now surrounded by a large park.

spots.name: Chaotian Palace
spots.summary: The Chaotian Palace is located in Nanjing, China. It was built as an imperial palace in the Ming dynasty, and today it is known as the Nanjing Municipal Museum. Chaotian Palace area has the largest preserved traditional Chinese architectural complex in Jiangnan.

spots.name: John Rabe House
spots.summary: The John Rabe House (拉贝故居), located at Xiaofenqiao No. 1 (小粉桥1号) in Nanjing, China, was where John Rabe lived during the Nanjing Massacre. In its garden, he protected more than 600 Chinese refugees from Japanese persecution.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.name: National Revolutionary Army Memorial Cemetery
spots.summary: The National Revolutionary Army War Memorial Cemetery in Nanjing was used for burials between 1931 and 1935. It is located at Purple Mountain in the east of Nanjing, and lies west of the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, occupying about one square kilometer.

spots.name: Yuejiang Tower
spots.summary: Yuejiang Tower is situated on the top of Shizishan to the northwest of downtown Nanjing, Jiangsu. The river referred to in its name is the Yangtze River, which may be viewed to the north, while central Nanjing can be viewed to the south.

spots.name: Jinling Hotel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Jinling Hotel Nanjing is a hotel in Nanjing, China, located near the city's Xinjiekou district. "Jinling" is an old name for Nanjing which is often used to refer to the city in a poetic context.

spots.name: Librairie Avant-Garde

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Librairie Avant-Garde is a bookstore opened by Qian Xiaohua in 2004, now regarded as the most representative bookstore in Nanjing, China.

spots.name: Hongshan Forest Zoo
spots.summary: Hongshan Forest Zoo is a zoological park in Nanjing, the capital city of Jiangsu province, China. The zoo is the member of the Chinese Association of Zoological Gardens. Located on 168 Heyan Road in the Xuanwu District of Nanjing, it is a 168.03 acres (68.00 ha) park and forest with 85% green coverage rate.

spots.name: Wutaishan Sports Center
spots.summary: Wutaishan Sports Center, named after the Mount Wutai, one of the most famed sacred mountain in Chinese Buddhism, is a sports center in Nanjing, China. It was established in 1952 and it was one of the oldest and most advanced stadiums in early time of People's Republic of China. It is home to the Wutaishan Stadium.

spots.name: Xu Garden
spots.summary: Xu Garden, also known as the West Garden and by other names, is a Chinese garden on the west side of the former Presidential Palace in Xuanwu District in central Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China. It and Zhan Garden are the two major gardens of the city.

spots.name: Jinjue Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jinjue Mosque is a mosque in Qinhuai District, Nanjing City, in the Jiangsu province of China.

spots.name: Nanjing Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nanjing Library is the third-largest library in China with over 10 million items. It houses important scientific, cultural and arts literature relating to Jiangsu province and other national historical records such as ancient Chinese and foreign publications.

photo.author: 吴 骋孜 from Shanghai, China

spots.name: Former Residence of Gan Xi
spots.summary: The Former Residence of Gan Xi, known as the Grand Courtyard of the Gan Clan, is located on Zhongshan South Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China. It lies next to Nan Bu Ting (南捕厅), the South station of the former Nanjing Police Station.

spots.name: Nanjing Great Hall of the People
spots.summary: The Nanjing Great Hall of the People, which serves as the Jiangsu Provincial People's Congress and the National Theatre of Drama and Music and Art Gallery, was built in 1936, and is located at No. 264, Changjiang Road, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Nanjing Great Hall of the People

spots.name: Jinghai Temple
spots.summary: Jinghai Temple is a 15th-century temple located in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China, to the southwest of Shizi Mountain. It was built to commemorate the voyage of Zheng He in the Ming Dynasty. The terms of the Treaty of Nanking were discussed in the temple.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception (圣母无染原罪始胎堂), commonly known as Shigu Road Cathedral (石鼓路天主教堂) to the locals, is a late 19th-century church in Nanjing that serves as the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Nanking. It is located in the centre of the city at 112 Shigu Road.

spots.summary: The Drum Tower of Nanjing on Gulou Mountain in the Gulou District of downtown Nanjing, was first built in the 15th year of the reign of Hongwu, founding emperor of the Ming Dynasty.

spots.name: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum Music Stage
spots.summary: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum Amphitheatre is a building affiliated to the complex of Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, located in the southeast of Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum Square in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: New Century Plaza is a tower complex located in Nanjing, China. Tower A, the main building, is a 255.2 meter (837 foot) tall skyscraper.

Jiangsu Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Jiangsu Art Gallery, also known as Jiangsu Provincial Art Museum, is a museum in Nanjing, in Jiangsu province in China. It was founded in 1936, during the Nanjing decade, as China's first state level museum. In 1960, it was formally renamed the Jiangsu Provincial Art Museum.

spots.name: Jiulong Bridge
spots.summary: The Jiulong Bridge is a historic stone arch bridge over the Qinhuai River in Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.

spots.name: China Gate Castle Park
spots.summary: China Gate Castle Park is a park in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, China. It is located north of the Qinhai River, south of the Nanjing City Wall and near the Changgan Bridge. Entrance to the treelined riverside park is gained through the China Gate.

spots.name: Tong Ren Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 1 Zhujiang, formerly known as the Tong Ren Tower, is a building in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. It is 186 meters (610 ft) tall with 53 floors. Construction began in 2003 and ended in 2007. The tower was designed by P & T Architects & Engineers Ltd. The building is used for offices, a hotel, and retail stores.

Xuanjin Bridge
spots.summary: The Xuanjin Bridge is a historic stone arch bridge over the moat of the Ming Palace in Qinhuai District, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.

spots.name: Former Shanghai Commercial and Savings Bank in Nanjing
Wutaishan Stadium
spots.summary: Wutaishan Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Wutaishan Sports Center, Nanjing, China. It is currently used mostly for football matches, as home ground of Nanjing City since 2024 and formerly for Jiangsu Ladies. The stadium has a capacity for 22,000 people.
